search_queries: targeted: expat, libxml2, mxml, yxml, libroxml, ezxml, sxmlc
ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations of the lead's runtime library binary package (max when two sonames are listed)
selection: expat (libexpat1 297,134) and libxml2 (libxml2 binary 290,724) are the two format-aware C XML parsers with the highest Debian popcon counts; both are verified. Homebrew 365-day installs give the same order (expat 1,360,500, libxml2 564,778).
uncertainty: Pilot cell: two third-party paths (expat 2.10.0 and libxml2 2.15.4) were built, matched the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls under LLVM source coverage, and have native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. They are distinct parser families. expat leads libxml2 by 6,410 installs (2.2%) on the binary-package metric, a near tie. The Debian sourcemax table would invert the order (libxml2 source 61,109) only because the libxml2 source now builds libxml2-16 and the older libxml2 binary is no longer attributed to it, so binary runtime-library counts are the primary metric; libxml2-16 (9,413) is not added because hosts may have both. Popcon counts installations, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not direct parser use. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'xml' (9 hits, 1 of them a C XML parser) plus seven targeted C names; Conan and Debian miss vendored single-file parsers. The control oracle (controls/xml/check_controls.py) uses Python's pyexpat, the same family as expat but not libxml2, so the libxml2 match is a cross-family check. The expat harness pins XML_SetHashSalt so AFL++ maps are reproducible; libxml2 needed no such change. ISO C documents no XML API. Two valid UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, encoding, XML 1.1 or rejection behaviour.
